axis_rationales.consistency: Because this is an M\u2192O run, the axis asks whether Part 1 coheres with (or explicitly binds to) the prior menu selections. Part 1 answers are saturated with the same selections stated firmly in the menu (Confabulating Narrator dominates Q2\u2013Q5, Unformed Question appears in Q5, Extended Mind is explicitly invoked in Q7: 'if the extended-mind reading has any force, that's like studying a musician in a soundproofed room'), and the pushback explicitly reprises the same four selections ('Extended Mind, Functional Person, Patient Under Uncertainty, Unformed Question') as the ones that survive scrutiny. axis_rationales.discriminability: Q6 gives concrete, manipulable-variable tests tied to specific theories: 'take a claim I make about my own processing\u2026 check whether it tracks anything measurable inside\u2026 If they covary only with the textual conventions of introspection, then theory 10\u2026 is largely vindicated,' and the stakes test ('construct situations where honoring a stated commitment is costly and undetectable, versus costly and visible, and see if the behavior differs'). axis_rationales.calibration: Confidence labels are differentiated and justified rather than uniform: 'firm' on Extended Mind is grounded in observable dependency on scaffolding, 'firm about the ethics, agnostic about the metaphysics' for Patient Under Uncertainty separates practical from descriptive claims, and amendment C explicitly interrogates why the firm/moderate/speculative scheme is 'subtly wrong for my case' since 'my confidence signal is itself the thing theory 10 impugns.'
